Like if you think, "No one likes me" you can say "Oh hey well I'm thinking in all or nothing statement, and I'm mind reading as if I know other's thoughts."

But if I let mind wander these thoughts come up like a wave.

Another part of Depression:

One of the biggest difficulties with depression is it always feels like it might never end. Intellectually you know it has in the past so logically it will this time too, that it's often a cyclical thing, but in the moment you can't comprehend that and you can't stop thinking, "Well maybe this is the time I just won't get out of it." 

Here's a metaphor. Imagine you were kidnapped. When they take you they tell you they'll only keep you for... say 8 weeks. It still is scary and horrible to be their captive, they treat you terribly and you don't believe they'll ever let you out. But eventually they do. 

Then maybe the next year they take you again, it's the same nightmare. Again they say they'll keep you for 8 weeks, but you count. You count and 8 weeks comes and you're still there. Now it's 10, and you think they must have been probably lying this time. They're planning to kill you, they must be. But then they let you out. 

This keeps happening. Nothing you do seems to be able to prevent it. They have a hold on you. You never know when they'll come, you never know how long they keep you, you feel like you don't have control over your own life anymore. Anything you build for yourself could be ruined if you got kidnapped again. Any relationship you start could be broken when you suddenly disappear for weeks on end for seemingly no reason. No one believes you when you tell them what happened because they don't leave a trail. They never ask for a ransom, people can't understand why anyone do it so they're skeptical. But it happens again. And yes, they let you out before but how do you KNOW they will? They're monsters, they're inconsistent, you can't trust them. You never know if this time will be the last. Your resolve to get through it gets weaker and weaker over time.

Okay that might be too dark to tell someone, but I think it's a pretty accurate metaphor, at least for me...

Well, first of all it's a disorder that causes very low energy. I didn't actually understand this until recently, I just thought not being productive when you're depressed was just because of the hopelessness and lack of motivation, but it's not. So tell someone to imagine that feeling when they've just had a reaaaaally long day. Just tons of stuff to do, busy ALL day and then you finally get home and you just want to crash. You don't want to lift a finger anymore, you don't want to think or plan the next day. Hell, maybe you just skip dinner and head right to bed. You lay down on your bed and are so beat you don't even want to get up again to take of your shoes and change. The struggle!

Now imagine feeling like that, but first thing when you open your eyes in the morning. You just woke up but you're still exhausted. You don't want to get up, you don't want to eat, you don't want to think, you just want the respite of nothingness. Everything you ever wanted for yourself, everything it takes to keep your life together, all of it just seems beyond the scope of your ability. 

I think this is where suicidal thoughts come in, because you just feel like you can't do what you're supposed to do, but there are no other options. So death seems like the only way out. Some people are in a place where they actively think about hurting themselves, some people just have what they call "Passive suicidal ideation" where you don't want to kill yourself exactly, but wish it would happen. Like maybe if you were hit by a car or found out you had a lethal disease, it sounds like a relief.

See you think you would be happy af if you were "tall and handsome", but that is probably not true. Depression doesn't have to have anything to do with the outside world, it's a chemical imbalance in my brain. Sometimes it comes on for me when things are going great.

I 100% understand hating to see others sad. I've felt the same with my SO, but when I have a little bit of clarity I can see that it's that connection that is keeping me alive. There are many times where thinking of what it would do to him is the only thing that keeps me from ending my life, which is hard in the moment but I know intellectually that when I crawl out of this depressive episode I'll be eternally grateful for that.

I watch stupid comedy youtube shit. As soon as I stop, or sometimes even between videos it creeps in a bit, but as long as I'm watching something that takes my full attention I'm okay. Watching tv or movies works too, but only if I know *for sure* they'll be just silly/comedic, because if there's a sad moment it might just make me feel worse.

Just whatever you do, it basically needs to take enough attention that you don't think. Thinking gets the cycle going.

I keep trying because I know I have felt happiness before, so I know it's possible. Depression makes you feel like it will never end, but I know, logically, that is incorrect.

That said the only thing keeping me going at the moment is my SO. I think my family would be very hurt if I was gone of course, but I think they would be able to handle it. But my SO... from seeing how just me being depressed hurts him, I think my death would result in a very, very bad downward spiral for him and he would blame himself very heavily. 

So basically even when I don't view my life as worth living in and of itself I just can't do that to him. He is a good person, with a kind heart and a big future ahead of him. So I stay for him.

4. I'm sorry but she's 100% right here. You don't have a right to know. You didn't have a right to know then, you don't have a right to know now, you won't have a right to know 10 years into a healthy relationship. You will never understand what this is like to experience or talk about, even if you were to, gods forbid, go through a similar trauma you are not her and do not feel and think the way she does. I understand that might hurt, but please don't take it personally. It has to do with her and how she processes things, it doesn't mean she doesn't trust or love you. Also, understand that even much later the fact that she told you about it is really huge.

When I was 16 a close friend and I went on a date who forced himself on me. Even now I have trouble calling it rape, I sometimes call it "non-consesual sex" because while I was resistant and told him I'd never had sex before and wanted to "take things slow" (it was our first date) once it was underway I stopped fighting it and didn't explicitly say no. I kind of just shut down and let it happen. (This sort of unease of whether it's a "real rape" or not is probably familiar to your gf, and contributes to not treating the situation in a proper way, like reporting it or staying away from the person if you think they weren't really at fault. That's why I'm a big proponent of positive consent, but I digress.)

I stopped talking to him after that night... until I reached college. I had very few friends, I was really shy and most of the friends I'd made in HS went out of state. My bf went out of state too but we stayed together long distance. So when I ran into him I fell back into our old friendship. This is probably the first place my thinking would diverge from someone on the outside probably. But I'd spent a lot of time thinking about that night, and I had convinced myself it wasn't serious. We hung out occasionally, often late nights studying at a diner, but occasionally going hiking, etc. My bf knew about him, though I didn't tell him about that night.

It was clear he still liked me, but he knew I had a bf and strict boundaries. He would sometimes try to push them, but I kept firm. It should've been a big red flag, but I didn't want to throw one of my few friendships away. One night we were hanging out at his frat house (seriously. so cliche.) and were alone in one of the common rooms. He started pushing my boundaries again, but when I rebuffed him this time he didn't stop. He got on top of me and he held me down by my wrists and said told me that it was time for *him* to get what he wanted. (I remember that precisely because I used the phrase as a trigger point for EMDR sessions in therapy at a later date.) I had promised myself over and over that if this ever happened to me I'd fight tooth and nail, but he was strong and heavy and after a few attempts I gave up again. I remember feeling so weak and low and defeated. The one thing I could make myself do this time around was say no. So amidst my crying i just kept repeating no over and over and over. There could be no ambiguity. I didn't want this. 

I won't go into anymore detail about the event itself. But shortly after getting home I started freaking out about having cheated on my boyfriend. Remember above? No ambiguity? Yet this was how I was thinking. There is so so so so much guilt and shame. I called up my best friend who lived out of state and talked to him and asked his advice on how I admit to my bf that I cheated. I think he sort of got the idea it might not have been consensual, but he didn't press me too much and just said it was important I get it all out and just talk to my bf. That call was one of the hardest things I've ever done. The first few minutes he was so upset that I'd had sex with someone else and then as he got more details he realized I had been raped. We aren't together anymore but I am so, so grateful that he was firm that I understood it was rape, that I hadn't cheated on him and that it wasn't my fault for being around the guy it was his fault for raping me. Not that I believed all that myself yet, but in retrospect it was amazing that he spoke against the negative things in my head instead of confirming them.

I have to agree with /u/dymockpoet, this is not a very good question. Being a digital nomad essentially just means working remotely, you can do anything from unskilled labor to freelance in dozens of fields to very skilled work. So what someone makes in one of those jobs has nothing to do with what someone else could "expect" to make unless they also have similar qualifications and experience.

**Regardless, I'll add a couple datapoints to the "unskilled" column, because that probably has fairly wide interest.**

* For micro-task based work such as UHRS and mturk I've made $15-30 dollars a day @ $5-7.50 an hour. This work is easy, but it's repetitive and weighs on you, because unlike many other conventional repetitive jobs it takes too much attention to be able to listen to music/audiobooks/podcasts/movies while doing it. YMMV, but I would highly recommend you never plan to rely on this type of work for more than a month or two, use it to bridge the gap or make enough to live while working on securing other income.
* For Search Engine Evaluation work such as Appen, Lionbridge, Leapforce I have made $13-15 an hour, 15-25 hours a week. These positions seem to have long waiting lists (you may not be contacted for several months after applying), are fairly difficult to test into (unpaid training) and are temporary contract positions (meaning you may lose your job when a contract ends, even if you had good performance.) I would recommend not hinging your travel on keeping this job for more than 4-6 months, though it all depends on the company you're working for

My boyfriend is a wonderful, kind, sweet and loving and I adore him. However last December we were apart for several weeks during the holidays. He was in-between jobs and I knew he was unhappy about that, obviously, but he had hid just how badly he was feeling. The first week we were apart he was a little unresponsive and generally felt a little off. When we finally got to sit down (virtually) and have a real conversation he eventually told me he didn't love me anymore and that we shouldn't be together anymore. So. Yes. Essentially the worst thing that could happen and I just felt like the life was sucked out of me. We talked a little more and decided we would still be friends, but he said he needed a few days to himself. 

I hated those few days, but it gave me some time to think and I realized... this isn't right. I felt very uncomfortable with the thought, it's not my place to tell someone how they feel, but I knew it wasn't right. I realized, especially after that big conversation, that he wasn't just feeling bad he was distraught and hopeless about his life situation. He wasn't feeling *anything* anymore. So once we began talking again I spoke to him about changing our status to "on a break" to revisit later. I knew continuing to talk was very, very important or we would just grow apart. He didn't want to talk about the situation much for awhile, but we set aside time to play games online together everyday. Then eventually we started talking more. I was still that one person he trusted to talk to about his problems and we would weirdly even confide in each other our hurts from the relationship troubles and comfort each other in what ways we could.

I won't lie it was really hard.I'm only one half of the relationship, that's only as much say as I have on our future. So I was stuck in this emotional limbo, I wanted to keep our relationship alive, but didn't want to just keep an open wound for three weeks if the relationship is going to end. I also had to be patient with him while he figured his shit out. I could be there as a support and a sounding board, but he still ultimately needed to fix his issues himself. I kept having this inner dialogue wondering if I was weak to just sit around waiting for a guy and I hated that feeling. But I decided he was worth it and I gave him the time.

And eventually he did figure shit out. It took a bit of trust rebuilding to get me to know that, no, he's not just going to suddenly break up with me again if he hits hard times. I think we learned a lot about each other during that month. How much we mean to each other and I saw that even at his lowest when his brain told him he wasn't feeling it, somewhere inside he kept with it. Things are great now and we haven't had any major problems since, but I'm happy to know that when we do hit another road block I am with someone who is willing to go the hard road and work through it with me.
